summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old male with a history of end-stage renal disease, coronary artery disease status post CABG and multiple stents, diabetes, and prior pacemaker explantation for bacteremia was admitted for acute chest pain radiating to the jaw, accompanied by diaphoresis, lightheadedness, and gastrointestinal symptoms. The pain was unresponsive to sublingual nitroglycerin but resolved with IV morphine. Evaluation showed stable troponin levels around 0.07, consistent with his baseline due to ESRD, and no new ischemic changes on EKG. Serial cardiac enzymes and clinical assessment ruled out acute coronary syndrome. He was treated for hyperkalemia with kayexalate and underwent hemodialysis on hospital day two. His symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home in stable condition with no medication changes, advised to follow up with cardiology and continue his regular dialysis schedule.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
Occlusion and stenosis of carotid artery without mention of cerebral infarction
